accepted.question_text: For the semilinear Dirichlet problem on an arbitrary open set Omega subset of R^d, given by -Delta u(x) = f(x, u(x), grad u(x)) for x in Omega and u(x) = 0 on the boundary of Omega, where f satisfies the coerciveness bound f(x, s, xi)s <= (lambda_1 - epsilon)s^2 + L|xi s| + h(x)|s| with epsilon > 0 and lambda_1 the optimal Poincare-Steklov constant, is the restriction L < L_max(epsilon, lambda_1) actually necessary for existence of weak solutions? Equivalently, if one allows L >= L_max(epsilon, lambda_1), must existence fail?
accepted.context_brief: Sharpness of the L < L_max(ε, λ_1) existence condition

evidence.quote: Let Ω ⊆ R^d be an arbitrary open set. We consider the following Dirichlet problem: -Δu(x) = f(x, u(x), ∇u(x)) (x ∈ Ω), u(x) = 0 (x ∈ ∂Ω).
The function f should satisfy a coerciveness and a growth condition (3) f(x, s, ξ)s ≤ (λ_1 - ε)s^2 + L |ξ s| + h(x)|s| ∀x ∈ Ω, s ∈ R, ξ ∈ R^d.
The positive constant L has to satisfy (5) L < L_max(ε, λ_1).

It is clear that in general we lose the existence of solutions for (2) if ε in condition (3) is allowed to be zero. Now we ask • Do we also lose the existence of solutions if L ≥ L_max (ε, λ_1)? Unfortunately we do not know the answer of this question.

accepted.question_text: For the generalized Robin boundary-value problem in which the a priori L^{q**} bounds are derived from an embedding of D(a_S) into L^p(Omega) together with Moser iteration, are those resulting L^{q**} a priori bounds best possible?
accepted.context_brief: Optimality of the Robin-setting L^{q**} a priori bounds

evidence.quote: Remark 12. One could ask if the Lq** a priori bounds derived from (24) by Moser iteration are the best possible. Indeed they are: [Dan00, Theorem 5.11.].
